title: Clamp Every Element In Place
statement:
Some functions exist to *change* what the caller passed in. In C++ that
means taking the argument by **non-const reference** -- and then actually
writing through it.

## Your function

```
void ClampAll(std::vector<int>& values, int lo, int hi);
```

Modify `values` in place so every element below `lo` becomes `lo` and
every element above `hi` becomes `hi`; elements already inside `[lo, hi]`
are left alone. `lo <= hi` always holds. `values` may be empty.

## Watch out

- **`for (int x : values)` iterates over *copies*.** Assigning to `x`
  changes the copy and nothing else -- the vector is untouched and the
  test fails without any error. Use `for (int& x : values)` (or index
  into the vector).
- **Return type is `void`.** The harness prints the vector you were given,
  not a returned one.
- C++17 provides `std::clamp(v, lo, hi)` in `<algorithm>`, if you want it.

tests.name: values on both sides of the window
a window of width zero flattens everything
